summary.text: An adolescent male presented with psychosis and a history of mild-to-moderate CPT II deficiency. He was born with low APGAR scores, fetal distress and jaundice and had a left-sided focal seizure shortly after birth requiring NICU stabilization. At 20-22 months a tonic-clonic seizure was likely precipitated by hypoglycemia secondary to poor feeding, and bilateral adrenal calcifications were found incidentally.

Testing after the seizure showed blood glucose down to about 30 mg/dL, essentially undetectable insulin, elevated free fatty acids and low free carnitine, and he was stabilized by dietary management. Metabolic testing for recurrent hypoglycemia showed elevated acylcarnitine, fibroblast probe studies showed elevated C16, and CPT2 activity was reduced by approximately 50%. He was diagnosed with mild-to-moderate CPT II deficiency and levocarnitine 3 g/day PO was initiated.

In adolescence he struggled with concentration and was placed on lisdexamfetamine, around that time developed persecutory delusions that persisted after the stimulant was stopped. Psychosis was stabilized with risperidone, aripiprazole, mirtazapine and benztropine; MRI showed occipital lobe encephalomalacia. Treatment moved to oral paliperidone and then a long-acting injectable, with sustained improvement and only sporadic ideas of reference and racing thoughts.

Whole-exome sequencing of the proband, unaffected fraternal twin and both parents found him homozygous for CPT2 p.Val368Ile and heterozygous for p.Met647Val, plus a heterozygous DBH splice variant from his father; Sanger sequencing of the DBH -970 region showed a TT genotype. None clearly explained his phenotype; orthostatic hypotension assessment was negative and further catecholamine testing was declined.

ambiguities.issue: The text states that the etiology of the phenotypes is unresolved: two independent phenotypes versus one complex presentation from a rare de novo variant, with the conclusion that the variants do not clearly explain the phenotypes.

evidence.quote: What is unknown from the medical record is whether the proband suffers from two independent clinical phenotypes—seizures caused by hypoglycemia and schizophrenia—or if all phenotypes are a complex presentation resulting from a rare de novo genetic variant not present in other immediate family members.
